violations.description: General employee practices. — --Food employee observed without proper hair restraint. Observed food employee without a hair restraint. Hair should be restrained in food prep areas.

Food supplies. — --Food item obtained from unapproved source. Home canned spicy bread and butter pickles found in the reach-in cooler in the kitchen. Home canned items are not approved for use in licensed kitchens.

Date marking and disposition of ready-to-eat potentially hazardous food. — --Refrigerated, ready-to-eat potentially hazardous food (prepared more than 24 hours ago) was not properly date marked. Multiple diced vegetables found in the refrigerated prep table in the front without date marked. Potentially hazardous food items should be dated so proper disposition can occur.

Variance requirement for specialized processing methods. — --Food establishment did not obtain approved variance or HACCP plan from regulatory authority for special process of vacuum sealing. Observed vacuum sealed meat in the reach-in freezer in the back storage area. Vacuum sealing must have a HACCP plan that has been approved by the South Dakota Department of Health Office of Health Protection. **Items should be discarded. The packages are not sealed properly.

Clean-in-place (CIP) equipment - Design and construction. — --Food contact surface of clean in place equipment was not cleaned properly. The inside of the ice machine was found dirty. This should be cleaned and maintained clean.

Cleaning frequency of equipment and utensils. — --Nonfood contact surface was not cleaned as frequently as required. Inside of the prep table and the bottom of the reach-in cooler were found dirty. These should be cleaned and maintained clean.

Handwashing lavatory supplies. — --Handwash lavatory was not supplied with supply of individual disposable towels, continuous towel supply system, or heated air-drying device. Hand washing sink was not provided with paper towels or other approved means for drying hands. Sinks should be supplied with an approved means for drying hands at all times. **Paper towels were provided during inspection.

Food display and service. — --Potentially hazardous food was not kept at an internal temperature of 41F or below during display or service. Partial package of sliced American cheese was found on the dish drain area of the 3 compartment sink at 45.8F. Potentially hazardous foods should be maintained below 41F or above 140F. **This was discarded.

Cleaning frequency of equipment and utensils. — --Nonfood contact surface was not cleaned as frequently as required. The insides of the microwave, reach-in freezer, and refrigerated prep table were found dirty. These should be cleaned and maintained clean.

Date marking and disposition of ready-to-eat potentially hazardous food. — --Refrigerated, ready-to-eat potentially hazardous food (prepared more than 24 hours ago) was not properly date marked. Diced peppers in the refrigerated prep table near the flat top grill were found not dated. Potentially hazardous foods should be date marked when held for more than 24 hours.

Cleaning frequency of equipment and utensils. — --Nonfood contact surface was not cleaned as frequently as required. The inside of upright freezer in the back room and the refrigerated prep table were found dirty. These should be cleaned and maintained clean.

Storage of cleaned equipment and utensils. — --Clean equipment/utensil was not stored in a clean, dry manner to protect from contamination. Clean utensils were found in dirty containers on the shelving unit in the kitchen. Clean equipment should be stored in a clean location, where they will be protected from contamination.

Laundering of linens. — --Laundry equipment was not located in area separated from exposed food or from exposed clean equipment/utensil. Dirty aprons were found stored on the shelving unit in the kitchen used for storing clean equipment and utensils. Dirty linens should be stored separated from clean linens and equipment.

Cleaning and maintenance of floors, walls and ceilings. — --Physical facilities (e.g. floors, walls, ceiling etc…) were not maintained in good repair. Tiles on the wall behind the refrigerated prep table were found missing during inspection. These should be replaced and maintained in good repair.

Employee dressing areas and lockers. — --Employees' clothing/possessions were in an area where contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens or single-service items may occur. Employee food items were found in the reach-in cooler in the kitchen as well as on top of the microwave. Personal items should be stored separated from food items used in the facility.
